court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, C.J. and G. Arul Murugan, J.)
appellants: D. Sangiliraj Proprietor, M/s. Tcs Leathers
respondents: Canara Bank Represented By Its Authorized Officer
advocates: For Petitioner: Mr. D. Prabhu Mukunth Arun Kumar Senior Standing Counsel
For Respondent: Mr. M.A. Abdul Wahab
prayer: Prayer: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a writ of mandamus Directing the respondent Bank to receive demand draft for Rs 14,18,841.50 as mentioned in E-Auction Notice dated 29-8-2024 and recall the E-Auction Notice dated 29-8-2024 and release/remove the encumbrance on the scheduled mentioned property mentioned in the E-auction notice.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari, C.J.:— When the writ petition was taken up for hearing, learned counsel on both sides submitted that the matter has been settled between the parties.

2. However, looking into the interim order passed by this Court on 9-7-2025, since the dues have been settled, the respondent Bank is directed to issue a “no encumbrance certificate” and also inform CIBIL about the same, forthwith.

3. With the above direction, the writ petition stands closed. There will be no order as to costs. Consequently, WMP No. 30223 and 30224 of 2024 are closed.
